STILLPOINT

BULLET TIME PHOTOGRAPHY
READ ME · macOS

1 Install

In the Stillpoint window, drag the Stillpoint icon onto the Applications folder.

After that you can eject the “Stillpoint” disk in the Finder sidebar and delete the downloaded file.

2 Open Stillpoint for the first time

Stillpoint is free and open source, but it is not registered with Apple, so the first time macOS blocks it. You only need to allow it once:

  1. Open the Applications folder and double-click Stillpoint. macOS says it could not verify the app. Click Done (or OK). Do not click “Move to Trash”.
  2. Open the Apple menu (top-left corner of the screen) and choose System Settings.
  3. In the sidebar, click Privacy & Security.
  4. Scroll down to Security. Next to the message about Stillpoint, click Open Anyway.
  5. Confirm with your password or Touch ID, then click Open Anyway once more.
From now on, Stillpoint opens normally with a double-click. After installing a new version, you may need to repeat these steps.

3 Take your first bullet time photo

  1. Connect your Canon cameras to the Mac with USB cables and turn them on. Stillpoint finds them by itself.
  2. Wait until every camera shows as connected. Some models take up to a minute.
  3. Click It’s bullet time. All cameras fire at the same instant.

Each shot appears as a session in Stillpoint. Click Save sessions to copy the photos to a folder you choose.

4 Requirements

  • Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) and macOS 13.3 or later.
  • Canon cameras supported by the Canon EDSDK. The camera software from Canon is already inside Stillpoint; you do not need to install anything else.
Help, updates and the list of supported cameras: github.com/astronaut954/stillpoint-bullet-time-photography
